title: Vibracore Survey of the Outer Shelf
text: Cores were retrieved using a vibracorer deployed from a shallow-draft vessel across twelve stations. Grain-size distribution was determined by laser diffraction granulometry, and the resulting spectra were deconvolved with an endmember mixing model. The dominant lithofacies is a moderately sorted quartzarenite exhibiting hummocky cross-stratification, consistent with storm-dominated deposition above fair-weather wave base. Recovery averaged 3.4 metres per station.

title: Radiocarbon Chronology of the Basin Fill
text: Fourteen accelerator mass spectrometry dates were obtained on articulated bivalve shells. Calibration used the Marine20 curve with a regional reservoir correction of 42 years. The resulting age-depth model indicates sedimentation rates rising sharply after 8.2 kiloyears before present, coincident with the onset of the modern circulation regime. Two dates were rejected as reworked on stratigraphic grounds.

title: Foraminiferal Assemblages and Palaeodepth
text: Benthic foraminiferal assemblages were counted at 5 centimetre resolution. The transition from an inner-shelf Ammonia-dominated assemblage to an outer-shelf Uvigerina assemblage marks a rapid deepening. Planktonic to benthic ratios corroborate the interpretation. Test preservation is excellent throughout, with no evidence of dissolution.

title: Seismic Stratigraphy of the Prograding Wedge
text: High-resolution boomer profiles image a prograding clinoform wedge with topset, foreset and bottomset geometry. Downlap surfaces are traceable across the survey area and define four seismic units. The lowermost unit onlaps an irregular acoustic basement interpreted as a subaerial unconformity. Vertical resolution is approximately 0.4 metres.

title: Heavy Mineral Provenance
text: Heavy mineral separates were prepared using sodium polytungstate at a density of 2.89 grams per cubic centimetre. Zircon, tourmaline and rutile indices point to a recycled orogenic source. Detrital zircon populations cluster at 1.0 and 1.8 gigayears, matching the exposed basement to the northwest rather than the volcanic arc to the south.

title: Organic Geochemistry and Terrestrial Input
text: Total organic carbon ranges from 0.3 to 2.1 weight percent. Carbon to nitrogen ratios above 20 in the lower interval indicate substantial terrestrial organic matter delivery, declining upward as marine productivity increases. Stable carbon isotope values shift from minus 26 to minus 21 per mille across the same interval.

title: Tidal Modelling of the Palaeo-Embayment
text: A depth-averaged hydrodynamic model was forced with reconstructed palaeobathymetry. Simulated tidal range in the embayment reaches 4.2 metres at spring tide, approximately double the modern value. Peak bed shear stress exceeds the threshold for fine sand transport across most of the basin floor, supporting the interpretation of a tidally reworked substrate.

title: Diagenetic Overprint in the Carbonate Interval
text: Cathodoluminescence petrography reveals three cement generations. The earliest is an isopachous fringe of high-magnesium calcite, succeeded by blocky low-magnesium calcite spar and finally by minor ferroan dolomite. Strontium isotope values of the earliest cement fall within the range expected for contemporaneous seawater, indicating early marine cementation.

title: Macrofaunal Community Structure
text: Grab samples yielded 84 macrofaunal taxa dominated by polychaetes and bivalves. Multivariate ordination separates three station groups corresponding to sediment texture rather than depth. Species richness is highest at intermediate mud content. The infaunal trophic index suggests no organic enrichment at any station.

title: Contaminant Loading in Surface Sediments
text: Trace metal concentrations were determined by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry after total digestion. Lead and zinc exceed effects-range-low guideline values at three nearshore stations. Enrichment factors normalised to aluminium indicate an anthropogenic component superimposed on a lithogenic background. Mercury remains below detection at all stations.

title: Sediment Budget and Coastal Retreat
text: A closed sediment budget was constructed for the littoral cell. Cliff recession supplies an estimated 41000 cubic metres per year, against a longshore transport capacity of 63000 cubic metres per year. The deficit is consistent with observed shoreline retreat averaging 0.6 metres per year over the last four decades, and implies the cell is not self-sustaining.

title: Machine Classification of Acoustic Backscatter
text: Multibeam backscatter mosaics were segmented using a random forest classifier trained on 240 ground-truth samples. Overall classification accuracy is 0.87 with a kappa statistic of 0.81. The principal confusion is between muddy sand and sandy mud, which the acoustic response does not separate cleanly. Class boundaries were smoothed with a majority filter.
